business_problem: Siemens needed to help industrial teams overcome fragmented engineering tools, labor shortages, and slow design and maintenance workflows so they could design, simulate, and operate complex products and factories faster and with less cost and risk.
solution_summary: Siemens integrated NVIDIA technologies across its industrial software and copilots so engineering, factory, and robotics users can work from one AI-enabled digital foundation. Teamcenter, Simcenter STAR-CCM+, and the Siemens Industrial Copilot use NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and CUDA for visualization, simulation, and digital twins, while NIM and NeMo microservices supply inference and agent capabilities. DGX B200 and H200 systems provide the training and serving horsepower behind industrial AI, and Jetson Thor, Isaac Sim, and Isaac Lab support robotics and physical-AI workflows. This stack lets Siemens simulate products, plants, and factories before they are built, ground copilots in operational context, and close the loop between visualization, prediction, and action. As a result, Siemens can reduce reactive maintenance work, speed design reviews, and support customers using digital twins and industrial AI to find issues earlier and operate assets more efficiently.

data_flow: Product and plant data is managed in Siemens engineering systems, simulated with GPU-accelerated tools, exposed through Omniverse-powered digital twins, and then consumed by copilots and robotics agents that return guidance, maintenance insights, and factory-optimization actions.
business_outcome: Siemens reports a 25% reduction in reactive maintenance time for workers using the Industrial Copilot, early pilots with 30% productivity improvement and potential for 50%, and customer deployments that surface up to 90% of issues before physical changes while improving throughput and lowering capex.
